## 1 Introduction {#s-1}

- 1 This document serves as a high-level framework that explains the EUDI Wallet certification system, ensuring its conformity with related regulations.
- 2 The certification system is based on the concept and content of the certification system described in ISO/IEC 17067 (see Figure 1).
- 3 NOTE 1: The terms "EUDI wallet" and "European Digital Identity Wallet" are used as synonyms.
- 4 NOTE 2: According to ISO/IEC 17000: “scheme” and “program” are synonyms.
- 5 The NL EUDI Wallet certification system aims to provide interested parties with information on the top-level certificate issuance in regards to European Digital Identity Wallets and the NL electronic identification scheme under which they are provided (Figure 2), in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2014/910 modified by 2024/1183 Article 5d(1).
- 6 A top-level certificate under the NL National eID Scheme will be subject to the applicant wallet provider to satisfy the applicable requirements of the certification scheme; to provide the required underlying certificates; and to demonstrate that it meets the national admission-conditions as set in National law.
- 7 All the underlying certificates indicated in Figure 2 and underlying certification schemes shall comply with ISO/IEC 17067 and ISO/IEC 17065.

Figure 2 Set of certificates/declarations of conformity resulting from implementation of the national EUDI Wallet certification system

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-sys-01/image_000001_91079d007d7d8262c94b024189ee421bfd9eae5dd5acaae808cafaaad9d2e3f7.png)

- 8 The figure illustrates the structural composition of the EUDI Wallet certification system, showing how the different certification schemes – functional, cybersecurity, and eID – combine to form the overall EUDI Wallet Provider Certificate (which will be issued per Wallet Provider).
- 9 Visually, the diagram is organized as a layered, modular architecture.
- (a) On the bottom / left side:
    - Functional certification of the Wallet Solution represents the set of conformity assessment activities related to wallet functionality as per Regulation (EU) 2014/910 modified by 2024/1183 (and related Implementing Acts) as-well-as compliance to onboarding flows requirements and compliance to PID issuance flow requirements. The expected activities for this certification mostly consist of product evaluation with functional testing.
- (b) On the bottom / middle
    - Cybersecurity certification of the Wallet Solution consists of at least two distinct external cybersecurity certification components i.e.: 1) the WSCA certificate and the WSCD certificate, both following the EUCC cybersecurity scheme, and 2) cybersecurity evaluation of Wallet Unit (Wallet Instance in combination with the WSCA/WSCD), based on a FITCEM evaluation scheme (in compliance with EN 17640:2022). The expected activities for this certification mostly consist of product evaluation with security testing.
- (c) On the bottom / right hand sides:
    - The wallet provider certification and the PID provider certification focus on the requirements for these providers outside the product certifications. This includes the technical, procedural and organizational requirements applicable to the services and service providers. The expected activities for this certification mostly consist of process evaluation and auditing

(d) On the top:

- o The NL Top Level Certification reflects the overall certificate of “The wallet and the eID-scheme under which the wallet is provided” as mentioned in the regulation. This is the certificate The Netherlands needs to provide to Europe for each combination of wallet and eID-scheme (PID-provider).
    - As the figure indicates, this certificate can only be issued if *and* the PID Provider has an activate certificate *and* the Wallet Provider has an active certificate *and* the Wallet provider demonstrates that it meets the national admission-conditions as set in National law.
- 10 Overall, the figure conveys how the certification system is architected as an integrated model, where several independent but interlinked certification schemes contribute to a harmonized and interoperable European Digital Identity Wallet certification outcome.

## 2 Legal and normative documents {#s-2}

- 11 In order to carry out certification of European Digital Identity Wallets, a certification system is established regarding compliance with Regulation (EU) 2014/910 modified by 2024/1183 on the basis of EN ISO/IEC 17067 and EN ISO/IEC 17065 standards and operated under the conformity assessment system as described in Regulation (EC) No 765/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 July 2008 setting out the requirements for accreditation and market surveillance relating to the marketing of products and repealing Regulation (EEC) No 339/93.
- 12 The NL EUDI Wallet Certification System and its schemes will demonstrate compliance with the following documents:
- (a) Regulation (EU) 2014/910 modified by 2024/1183 Functional framework (Article 5a) and respective Commission Implementing Regulations:
    - EU 2024/2977
    - EU 2024/2979
    - EU 2024/2982
- (b) Certification Rules (Article 5c of with Regulation (EU) 2014/910 modified by 2024/1183) and the Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981
- (c) European Cybersecurity Certification scheme as specified in EUCC as defined in the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482
- (d) Article 54 of the EU 2019/881 Cybersecurity Act
- (e) Article 8(3) of EU 910/2014 on eID and trust services for electronic transactions along with Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502
- (f) Regulation (EU) 765/2008 setting out the requirements for accreditation and market surveillance relating to the marketing of products(..), in particular Articles 4 and 5.
- 13 In addition, the EUDI Wallet Certification System will comply with:

## 3 Governance and stakeholder relationships {#s-3}

### 3.1 Stakeholders {#s-3-1}

- 14 This section briefly describes the stakeholders involved in the NL EUDI Wallet Certification System, their roles and responsibilities.

#### 3.1.1 System Owner {#s-3-1-1}

- 15 Role: Top-level governance body of the certification system.
- 16 Owner: Minister of Economic Affairs (in close concertation with Minister of the Interior)
- 17 Responsibilities:
    - Define the overall rules of the certification system.
    - Define the overall evaluation methods and requirements
    - Maintain and update system documentation and make it available to all relevant stakeholders
    - Ensure the overall system complies with ISO/IEC 17067 and legal requirements
    - Notify the certification system to the EDICG for opinions and recommendations as required in the regulation.
    - Cooperate with other EU Member States operating an EUDI Wallet certification system to ensure a level playing field towards a future EU certification system

#### 3.1.2 Top-Level Scheme Owner {#s-3-1-2}

- 18 Role: Governance of Top Level Certification Scheme
- 19 Owner: Minister of Economic Affairs (in close concertation with Minister of the Interior)
- 20 Responsibilities:
    - Define elaborate scheme requirements
    - Maintain scheme-specific documentation and make it available to all relevant stakeholders
    - Ensuring compliance with the NL Certification System rules/methods/requirements
    - Supervision of certification activities
    - Compliance of certified services with national and EU legal frameworks
    - Post-certification monitoring, particularly following incidents or vulnerabilities
- 21 NOTE: The roles of System Owner and Top level Scheme Owner can be combined.

#### 3.1.3 Subordinate Scheme Owners {#s-3-1-3}

- 22 Role: Governance of subordinate certification schemes for specific products or services
- 23 Owners: For some subordinate schemes, individual CABs may propose their own scheme if legal requirements allow and if their scheme is in full compliance with NL Certification System, top-level scheme and set requirements for the subordinated schemes (methods and related requirements). Where EUCC is available and mandated, the legal ownership of the EUCC scheme applies
- 24 Responsibilities:
    - Define practical scheme details and operations
    - Maintaining scheme-specific documentation and make it available to all relevant stakeholders
    - Ensuring compliance with the rules/methods/requirements of the NL Certification System and all overarching schemes applicable to the subordinate scheme
    - Supervision of certification activities
    - Post-certification monitoring, particularly following incidents or vulnerabilities

#### 3.1.4 National Accreditation Body (NAB) {#s-3-1-4}

- 25 Role: Ensures trust and competence of Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs).
- 26 Responsibilities:
    - Accredit CAB-CB according to ISO/IEC 17065 or other standards, if required by the scheme
    - Accredit CAB-ITSEF according to ISO/IEC 17025, in respective certification schemes
    - Verify competence, impartiality, and consistent application of certification rules
    - Act under the EU’s overarching accreditation framework (Regulation 765/2008).

#### 3.1.5 Conformity Assessment Body (CAB-CB) {#s-3-1-5}

- 27 Role: Performs or subcontracts conformity assessment activities.
- 28 Responsibilities:
    - Conduct or subcontract evaluations, audits, or testing
    - Produce or validate test reports, evaluation reports, and certification documentation
    - Support decision-making on conformity findings.

#### 3.1.6 Conformity Assessment Body (CAB-ITSEF) {#s-3-1-6}

- 29 Role: Performs evaluation or testing activities.
- 30 Responsibilities:
    - Conduct evaluations or testing
    - Produce test reports, evaluation reports, and evaluation documentation
    - Support the CAB-CB decision-making on conformity findings.

#### 3.1.7 Applicant / Certificate Holder {#s-3-1-7}

- 31 Role: An entity seeking certification or possessing the certificate. Typically, the EUDI Wallet provider, PID provider or their subcontractors and suppliers
- 32 Responsibilities:
    - Submit the application for certification
    - Provide all required technical, procedural, and security documentation
    - Continuously maintain conformity throughout operation (including post-certification obligations).
- 33 NOTE: each certificate applicant/holder is responsible for the costs related to the certification process and maintenance of their own certificate

#### 3.1.8 European Digital Identity Cooperation Group (EDICG) {#s-3-1-8}

- 34 Role: EU-level coordination and harmonization of the European Digital Identity Framework
- 35 Responsibilities:
    - Support consistent implementation of the EUDI Wallet framework across Member States.
    - Facilitate cooperation between national authorities, including on supervision, incident handling, and cross-border interoperability.
    - Provide guidance to ensure uniform application of certification-related requirements.
    - Assist the European Commission in monitoring and improving the functioning of the European Digital Identity ecosystem.

#### 3.1.9 Supervisory Authority (SA) {#s-3-1-9}

- 36 NOTE: SA may not be merged with the System/Scheme Owner role. Different organizational units of the Ministry of Digital Affairs have been assigned to these roles.
- 37 Role: Supervisory and oversight function, according to EU and national law
- 38 Responsibilities:

    - Supervision of Trust Framework (see NL-SYS-03)
    - Cross-border cooperation and notification processes.

## 4 Mandatory elements of the scheme definition based on ISO/IEC 17067 {#s-4}

### 4.1 Scheme ownership {#s-4-1}

39 NOTE: the text is relevant for System Owner and Scheme Owners.

40 In accordance with Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981, Chapter II, Article 3(1) on the establishment of national certification schemes, Member States shall assign a Scheme Owner for each national certification system.

- 41 The owner of the top-level national EUDI wallet certification scheme is the Minister of Economic Affairs (in close concertation with Minister of the Interior).
- 42 The Top-Level Scheme owner and subordinate Scheme Owners need to:
- (a) take on full responsibility for the objectives, the content and the integrity of the scheme;
- (b) maintain the scheme and provides guidance when required;
- (c) set up a structure for the operation and management of the scheme;
- (d) document the content of the scheme;
- (e) ensure that the scheme is developed by people competent in both technical and conformity assessment aspects;
- (f) plan to protect the confidentiality of information provided by the parties involved in the scheme;
- (g) operate and maintain the risk register defined in CIR (EU) 2024/2981;
- (h) evaluate and manage the risks/liabilities arising from its activities;
- (i) approve the scope of subcontracting activities outsourced by the certification body;
- 43 Scheme Owners may subcontract a defined part of their tasks to a third party. When subcontracting the third party, the Scheme Owner shall set out the duties and responsibilities of all parties by contract. Scheme owners shall remain responsible for all subcontracted activities performed by their subcontractors.
- 44 Scheme Owners shall monitor the compliance of CAB-CB with their obligations pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2014/910 modified by 2024/1183 and pursuant to the national certification schemes.
- 45 Scheme Owners shall perform their monitoring activities, if applicable, at least based on the following information:
- (a) information coming from certification bodies (CAB-CB), testing laboratories (CAB-ITSEF), national accreditation bodies, and relevant market surveillance authorities, if applicable;
- (b) information resulting from its own or another authority’s audits and investigations;
- (c) complaints and appeals received.

- 46 Scheme Owners shall manage the scheme during its life cycle and have procedures for reviewing and improving the scheme based on:
- (a) information gathered from EUDI Wallet ecosystem stakeholders, including but not limited to CABs, Wallet Providers, other Member States and EUDI Wallet Cooperation Group;
- (b) its own monitoring activities;
- (c) the complaint and appeal processes;
- (d) outcomes from internal procedures.
- 47 Scheme Owners shall maintain procedures or references to the applicable national legislation, which defines the mechanism to effectively lodge and handle complaints and appeals in relation to their implementation of the certification scheme or to a certificate of conformity issued. These procedures shall include the provision of information to the complainant about the progress of the proceedings and on the decision taken, and information to the complainant on the right to an effective judicial remedy.
- 48 The certification schemes shall contain provisions that all complaints and appeals that have not been resolved by the CAB-CB are sent to the Scheme Owner for assessment and resolution.
- 49 Scheme Owners shall inform NL Certification System / NL-Top-Level Certification Scheme Owner of revisions to the certification scheme. That notification shall provide adequate information to issue recommendations to the Scheme Owner and opinions about the updated certification scheme.
- 50 Where applicable, the NL Certification System / NL-Top-Level Certification Scheme Owner shall notify such changes to the EDICG. That notification shall provide adequate information for the Cooperation Group to issue recommendations and opinions about the updated certification scheme.
- 51 The Top-Level Scheme Owner shall publish a list of certified EUDI Wallet solutions along with information specified in CIR (EU) 2024/2981 Annex V and ensure this list remains accurate and current.

### 4.2 Scope and objectives {#s-4-2}

- 52 The NL EUDI Wallet Certification System addresses the object of certification defined in CIR 2024/2981, art. 3(2) and 3(3).
- 53 The certification system consists of the general approach of assessing the conformity of European Digital Identity Wallets and the electronic identification scheme under which they are provided as defined in CIR 2024/2981.
- 54 The legally required overall certification of “the digital identity wallet and the eID scheme under which the wallet is provided”, is defined as one top-level scheme composing certificates from three distinct subordinate certification schemes (see Figure 3):
- European Digital Identity Wallet Functional Certification Scheme (NL-CS series)
- European Digital Identity Wallet Cybersecurity Certification Scheme (NL-CS series)

- National eID Scheme Certification Scheme (NL-P-P and NL-P-W series)
- 55 This document provides an overview of how this structure, and its elements, are nested and meet the specific requirements of the relevant standards and regulations, to reach a top-level European Digital Identity Wallet certification.
- 56 Each certification scheme is building on top of necessary standards (international or European) or technical specification references that constitute a set of specified requirements for the scheme 1 .
- 57 Each scheme is based on the ISO/IEC 17067 product 2 certification scheme type. The types assigned to EUDI Wallet certification scheme are the following (as defined in ISO/IEC 17067):
- European Digital Identity Wallet Functional Certification Scheme (Type 5);
- European Digital Identity Wallet Cybersecurity Certification Scheme (Type 5);
- National eID Scheme Certification Scheme (Type 6).
- 58 European Digital Identity Wallet Functional Certification Scheme (NL-FS series) lists a set of requirements and necessary information to allow conformity assessment to be performed on the software/hardware components of the EUDI Wallet Unit. It establishes one certificate /declaration of conformity for a specific wallet solution as provided by a wallet provider.
- 59 European Digital Identity Wallet Cybersecurity Certification Scheme (NL-CS series) provides requirements and necessary information to allow conformity assessment for a specific wallet solution as provided by a wallet provider.
- 60 eID Certification Scheme (NL-P-P- and NL-P-W-series) is an overarching scheme providing guidance and necessary information to allow conformity assessment to be

## 5 Scheme life cycle management {#s-5}

### 5.1 Conditions for participation of CABs in the certification scheme {#s-5-1}

63 Any CAB is required to successfully pass an accreditation process within the scope of relevant certification scheme. The CAB shall inform the Scheme Owner about the accreditation status without undue delay.

- 64 In duly justified cases, the CAB may start performing its evaluation or certification services according to the rules specified in NL-SYS-05, Section 10.
- 65 For evaluating requirement covered in the accreditation, the Scheme Owner shall rely on the NAB accreditation process as-well-as on surveillance towards accredited CABs.
- 66 The CAB shall inform the Scheme Owner of any change in the status of the CAB accreditation without undue delay.

### 5.2 General rules on certification processes {#s-5-2}

- 67 Top-Level Certification of the EUDI Wallet Provider shall be performed under NL-TLcertification scheme, building on relevant certificates or declaration of conformity from NL-TL, NL-FS, NL-CS, NL-P-P/W
- 68 While submitting the application for the top-level certificate, the Wallet Provider is required to submit all relevant certificates and corresponding certification reports for the respective subordinate certification schemes. The CAB-CB shall assess the scope and validity of these certificates and verify that the applicant meets the conditions to be recognized/admitted to operate as a wallet provider under the NL Wallet eIDscheme before issuing a top-level certificate
- 69 Dependencies among statuses of certificates issued are specified in relevant sections of respective certification scheme descriptions (NL-TL, NL-FS, NL-CS, NL-P-P/W ).

### 5.3 Assurance evidence from external sources {#s-5-3}

- 71 The CAB may rely on external assurance evidence in all certification schemes and in reference to the top-level certificate. The status of assurance cases shall be considered as the assurance outcome:
- Full reliance. The assurance evidence provides sufficient evidence that the requirement is met. No supplementary evaluation activities are required for this requirement. The CAB-CB shall document the basis for this determination.
- Partial reliance. The assurance evidence covers part of the requirement or provides a level of assurance that requires supplementation. The CAB-CB shall specify and perform the necessary supplementary evaluation activities as part of the evaluation.

- No reliance. The assurance evidence is not available, is not adequate, or does not cover the requirement. The CAB-CB shall perform its own evaluation of the requirement in full.
- 72 The CAB-CB shall document its evaluation and determination of reliance for each piece of assurance evidence as part of the evaluation records. The CAB-CB remains fully responsible for the certification decision regardless of the extent to which reliance is placed on external assurance evidence.
- 73 Acceptance of assurance evidence in the evaluation process may not contradict the requirement of ISO/IEC 17065, 7.4.5 related to the evaluation results related to certification completed prior to the application for certification.

### 5.4 Surveillance {#s-5-4}

- 74 The top-level certificate is subject to annual surveillance activities performed by the CAB-CB according to the rules specified in NL-SYS-03 certification scheme and considering the outcomes from surveillance activity specified under NL-FS, NL-CS, NLP-P/W certification schemes
- 75 Surveillance activities relevant to the object of certification are specified in respective certification schemes.

### 5.5 Post-certification obligations of certificate holders {#s-5-5}

- 76 The certificate holder shall:
- comply with relevant European and national legislation related to the EUDI Wallet Solution including but not limited to CIR 2024/2981;
- establish, implement and maintain communication channels with CAB-CBs, CABITSEFs if applicable, and the Scheme/System Owner to fulfill its notification obligations;
- ensure that essential information related to the secure use, certification and updates of the EUDI Wallet solution in relation to the certified service or the certified part of product is available to end users in an accessible and understandable language and is presented in a format which is appropriate to its function;
- establish, implement and maintain a continual process of identification, analysis and assessment of vulnerabilities that can affect the EUDI Wallet solution in relation to the certified service or the certified part of product or other products or services that support the EUDI Wallet solution;
- establish, implement and maintain vulnerability handling procedures and cooperate with the CAB-CB and the Scheme Owner in case the vulnerability is identified in relation to the certified service or the certified part of product, or other products or services that support the EUDI Wallet solution;

- publish or reference to publicly known vulnerabilities that can affect the EUDI Wallet solution, and relate to the certified service or certified part of the product, or other products or services that support the EUDI Wallet solution;
- ensure that published or referenced information:
    - clearly identify the vulnerability,
    - indicate the affected versions of the product, or the part of it, or any other product or service that supports the EUDI Wallet solution,
    - contain a description of the mitigating or updating measures that are available for relevant stakeholders,
    - does not contain any details that allow direct or indirect exploitation.
- use the mark of conformity in relation to the EUDI Wallet solution, the certified service or the product that contains certified parts, according to the rules provided in NL-SYS-03.

### 5.6 Changes to the object of top-level certification {#s-5-6}

- 77 Changes that have impact on the EUDI Wallet solution, thus on the top-level certificate shall be handled under the CAB-CB regular change management process which is a part of the certificate maintenance process (see Figure 4).
- 78 In case the process is initiated by the Certificate Holder the CAB-CB shall be notified accordingly and obtain the description of changes in the form of Impact Analysis Report (IAR).
- 79 The processes of IAR handling by the CAB-CB are described in respective certification schemes.

Figure 4 Change management process implemented in the certification system

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-sys-01/image_000003_ae9b1c020cbbcc34350fe8757964237f3c08b3dfabfb21b9be9b290f81d4326d.png)

- 80 Following the flow presented in Figure 4, any change that results from a security incident or vulnerability shall be handled by the CAB-CB with respect to the assurance continuity principle.
- 81 NOTE: NL-SYS-03 contains the description of technical vulnerability handling from the Scheme Owner perspective.

### 5.7 Dealing with non-conformities {#s-5-7}

- 82 Any non-fulfillment of specified requirement by the object of certification shall be considered as a nonconformity.
- 83 NOTE: Due to different characteristics of nonconformities in certification schemes specific provisions are included in NL-TL, NL-FS, NL-CS, NL-P-P/W, respectively.
- 84 The CAB-CB shall ensure that any non-compliance identified in relation to the certificate holder obligations are handled in accordance with the contract provisions and ISO/IEC 17065.
- 85 In case where the CAB-CB identifies that the certificate holder does not comply with the obligations imposed on the entity by the applicable European, or national regulations or contractual provisions, the CAB-CB shall:
- Formally notify the certificate holder of the existence of the non-compliance, describing:
    - the specific obligation - suspected or proven - to be breached,
    - available evidence,
    - possible impact on trust or maintenance of certification.
- Request from the certificate holder further clarifications of the case,
- In case the certificate holder clarification is not sufficient, establish a maximum period, which may not exceed thirty (30) calendar days, within the certificate holder shall:
    - propose appropriate corrective measures, and
    - commit to its execution within a reasonable time.
- 86 Upon failure to comply with the deadline, or unsatisfactory proposals, or failure to respond the CAB-CB enters the procedure of suspension of the certificate in accordance with section 5.8.

### 5.8 Suspension, termination, withdrawal or expiration of certificates {#s-5-8}

- 87 A certificate may be suspended or withdrawn as the result of finding nonconformities in certified object or part of it.

- 88 Where the certificate is withdrawn or terminated on request of the Certificate Holder, such action shall be final, and the certificate shall not be reinstated. The withdrawal of the certificate shall not automatically invalidate certificates issued for individual components, provided that such component certificates remain compliant with the applicable requirements.
- 89 Where the certificate is suspended, the certificate may be reinstated following a formal certification process. Such a process shall demonstrate that the causes leading to the suspension have been adequately addressed and resolved and that continued conformity with the certification requirements is ensured.
- 90 The CAB shall inform the Certificate Holder, the System Owner and the top-level scheme owner of the date of expiration certificate and take appropriate action toward re-certification without undue delay.
- 91 NOTE 1: Expiration of top-level certificate of one Wallet Provider and/or one Wallet Solution does not have any impact on validity of other certificates issued under the NL EUDI Wallet Certification System.
- 92 NOTE23: The CAB-CB follows requirements of ISO/IEC 17065 to ensure discontinuity of relationship between the product or service concerned and certification.

### 5.9 Complaints and appeals {#s-5-9}

- 93 Any certification decision, including decisions related to suspension or withdrawal of the certificate, may be appealed by a relevant stakeholder identified within the certification system, as well as by a user of an EUDI Wallet. Appeals shall be duly substantiated by reference to the applicable legal requirements, scheme requirements, or system requirements that are alleged not to be fulfilled.
- 94 An appeal shall be handled by relevant CAB-CB according to the CAB-CB publicly available procedures.
- 95 The Scheme Owner may not alter CAB decisions.
- 96 Any EUDI Wallet stakeholder may submit a complaint to the Scheme Owner regarding any aspect of NL EUDI Certification System.
- 97 A complaint may be handled under the provisions of administrative procedure regarding complaints and requests.
- 98 NOTE 1: NL-SYS-03 contains the description of complaint or appeal cases that are handled by the Scheme Owner.
- 99 NOTE 2: Respective scheme documents contain description of appeal cases that are handled by the CAB-CBs.

### 5.10 Retention of records {#s-5-10}

- 100 The validity period of top-level certificate and wallet provider and PID-provider certificate is four years (see NL-TL, NL-P-P/W).

- 101 The retention period of records created during the certification process shall be defined according to relevant legal requirements which will include provisions so that records related to NL-TL, NL-P-P/W and NL-FS/CS-certification shall --in addition to local backups-- also be given in custody at the Certification System Owner.
- 102 NOTE 1: It is recommended to specify the retention period for all relevant records that are created per each certification case as not less than five years after the certification validity has expired.
- 103 NOTE 2: The certification case encompasses all relevant CAB initiatives regarding the application or the certified product.

### 5.11 Periodic review of the certification scheme {#s-5-11}

- 104 The NL Certification System Owner shall perform periodic reviews of the EUDI Wallet certification system and certification schemes which operate under the system.
- 105 NOTE: Periodic review procedures for the Scheme Owner are specified in NL-SYS-03 document.

### 5.12 Scheme maintenance {#s-5-12}

- 106 In the case the review process (internal or in the form of peer review) identifies noncompliances in the scheme or the system performance does not meet defined criteria the Scheme Owner shall initiate the scheme maintenance process which could result in changes in the system or scheme themselves, including their documentation.
- 107 NOTE: The scheme maintenance process is described in NL-SYS-03.
- 108 When the certification system or top-level scheme introduces new or revised requirements the System Owner or Scheme Owner shall ensure this information is made available to all relevant stakeholders,
- 109 Following information from the System Owner or Scheme Owners, the CAB-CB shall ensure the changes that affect the client are communicated to all clients. The CAB-CB shall verify the implementation of the changes by its clients, if applicable, and shall take actions introduced by the scheme due to the changes.
- 110 NOTE 2: Possible actions toward changes affecting certification are presented in ISO/IEC 17065, 10.1.3.

## 6 Conformity assessments methods, specifications, and reporting overview {#s-6}

### 6.1 General {#s-6-1}

- 111 This chapter provides a unified overview of the conformity assessment toolbox that supports the EUDI Wallet certification scheme. It establishes the methods, competence requirements, decision criteria, and reporting rules that underpin all activities across the functional, cybersecurity, and national eID scheme certification schemes.
- 112 General description of applicable conformity assessment methods is contained in Annex A.

### 6.2 Required elements to be defined within conformity assessment methods {#s-6-2}

- 113 To ensure harmonized implementation, each method applied within the scheme shall explicitly define the following elements:
- Competence requirements: Competence shall be defined for all individuals involved in the assessment, based on the method which is applicable to relevant certification scheme.
- Outsourcing conditions: As a rule, outsourcing is not permitted unless explicitly allowed within the method’s normative framework. Where permitted, the applicable requirements shall be described in relevant certification scheme.
- Pass/Fail criteria: For each assessment activity, the method shall define the applicable pass/fail criteria and describe their impact on the validity of the certificate.

### 6.3 Mandatory elements of reports {#s-6-3}

- 114 Mandatory elements of reporting shall be defined according to the conformity assessment method. The certification scheme can add other relevant requirements, if applicable.
- 115 Test reports include the following mandatory elements (see ISO/IEC 17025 for reference):
- Title: test report / report on sampling;
- Name and address of the testing laboratory;
- Location of performance of the laboratory activities;
- Unique identification that all its components are recognized as a part of a complete report, and a clear identification of the end;
- Name and contact details of the customer;
- Identification of the method;
- Dates of performance of the laboratory activity;
- Date of issue of the report;
- Statement to the effect that the results relate only to the items tested or sampled;
- Results with, where appropriate, the units of measurements;
- Identification of the person(s) authorizing the report;

- Clear identification when test results are from external providers, including customers.
- 116 The management system audit report shall include the following mandatory elements (see ISO/IEC 17021-1):
- Identification of the certification body;
- The name and address of the client and the client’s management representative;
- The type of audit (e.g. initial, surveillance or recertification audit);
- The audit criteria;
- The audit objectives;
- The audit scope, particularly identification of the organizational or functional units or processes audited and the duration of the audit;
- Identification of the audit team leader, audit team members and any accompanying persons;
- The dates and places where the audit activities (onsite or offsite) were conducted;
- Audit evidence, findings and conclusions, consistent with the required elements of the audit;
- Any unresolved issues, if identified.
- 117 Documentation for product-, service- or process – related certification which is provided to the client shall include the following mandatory elements (see ISO/IEC 17065):
- The name and address of the certification body;
- The date certification is granted (the date shall not precede the date on which the certification decision was completed);
- The name and address of the client;
- The scope of certification;
- The term or expiry date of certification, if certification expires after an established period;
- 118 Additionally, the certification report for the object of conformity shall include specific information required by the certification schemes (see NL-TL, NL-FS, NL-CS, NL-PP/W).

### 6.4 Conformity assessment template dedicated to certification schemes {#s-6-4}

- 119 To ensure consistent implementation of the certification schemes the table of basic characteristics of the scheme is introduced.

| Subject                           | Description required                                                                                                                   | Required details                               |
|-----------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| Object of conformity assessment   | Clear identification of the component that is assessed                                                                                 | Reference to the composite model when relevant |
| Conformity assessment methodology | Choice of methodology out of the methodologies described in Annex A                                                                    | Rationale to use this methodology              |
| Impartiality criteria             | Identification of impartiality criteria only when they add to the general impartiality criteria of the conformity assessment standard. |                                                |
| Confidentiality criteria | Identification of confidentiality criteria only when they add to the general impartiality criteria of the conformity assessment standard. |                                                                            |
| Competence requirements  | People performing conformity assessment methods.                                                                                          | Specification of competence requirements or reference to relevant sources. |
| Pass/Fail Criteria       | Pass/Fail criteria general description                                                                                                    | Reference to relevant standard(s) or WM-0x documents                       |
| Certificate lifecycle    | Suspension / withdrawal/renewal criteria when relevant                                                                                    | Condition description in all respective certification schemes              |
| Reporting                | Reporting elements reference to 6.3 + additional elements where required                                                                  | Details on the format                                                      |
| Dependencies             | Dependencies on other objects of conformity assessment                                                                                    | Description                                                                |

## 7 Conformity analysis {#s-7}

### 7.1 Conformity with eIDAS regulation and relevant implementing acts {#s-7-1}

#### 7.1.1 Conformity with implementing act (CIR (UE) 2024/2981) {#s-7-1-1}

- 120 The EUDIW Certification System and EUDIW Certification Scheme is designed to be fully compliant with the specifications and procedures established by the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2981 for the certification of European Digital Identity Wallets. The following analysis details how the requirements of the implementing act are met by the certification scheme structure.

## 121 Article 1: Subject matter and scope {#s-121}

- 122 Requirement: Sets the scope for a robust framework for the certification of wallets
- 123 Conformity: The entire certification system, governed by NL-SYS-01, is designed to establish such framework. The pillars (NL-TL; NL-FS, NL-CS, NL-P-P/W) collectively cover the full scope required for the certification of the EUDI wallet solution and its underlying eID system.

## 124 Article 2: Definitions {#s-124}

- 125 Requirement: Provides key definitions for the regulation.
- 126 Conformity: NL-SYS-02 (Vocabulary) is a dedicated document for establishing a set of terms relevant to the certification scheme. NL-SYS-02 incorporates all definitions from Article 2 of CIR (EU) 2024/2981 and adds relevant terms and their definitions, if necessary.

## 127 Article 3: Establishment of national certification schemes {#s-127}

- 128 Requirement 3(1): Member States shall assign a Scheme Owner.
- 129 Conformity: NL-SYS-01 assigns the System Owner/Scheme Owner and specifies responsibilities of these roles. This role will be assigned by national legislation.
- 130 Requirement 3(2): The object of certification shall be the provision and provisioning of wallet solutions and the national eID scheme under which they are provided.
- 131 Conformity: This is fully covered by the three-pillar structure:
- NL-FS Series: Covers the functional certification of the EUDI Wallet solutions.
- NL-CS Series: Covers the cybersecurity certification of the EUDI wallet solutions.
- GP-NLWP/PP Series: Covers the certification of the underlying eID scheme (aka the wallet providers and the PID providers)
- 132 Requirement 3(3): The object of certification shall include specific elements.

- 133 Conformity:
- Software components: Addressed by NL-FS-series, NL-CS-series (incl specific Wallet Instance FITCEM PP and WSCA PP PP) en Resilience requirements related to software development and the provisioning of essential services under the NL-P-P/W-series).
- Hardware components: Addressed by a Protection Profile for WSCD, certified externally.
- Processes that support the provision and operation of a wallet solution and explicitly referenced in CIR (EU) 2015/1502: Addressed in detail by the the NL-P-P/W-series notably the requirements on “Wallet Onboarding & LifeCycle Management” and “PIDissuance and lifecycle management).

## 134 CHAPTER II NATIONAL CERTIFICATION SCHEMES {#s-134}

- 135 Requirement 3(4): National certification schemes shall include a description of the specific architecture of the wallet solutions and of the electronic identification scheme under which they are provided.
- 136 Conformity:
- 137 See Annex B in this document.

- 139 Conformity:
- the specific architecture of a wallet solution and of the electronic identification scheme: see Annex B of this document.

- evaluation plan(s) drawn-up in accordance with section 7.4.1 of EN ISO/IEC 17065;2012: The Certification System states the object of certification, provides a structured decomposition of the object of certification, including elements where component certifications are possible, sets the evaluation methodologies and lists a set of requirements (derived from various risk analysis) across NL-FS-, NL-CS and NL-PP/W-series.
- the security requirements necessary to address the cybersecurity risks and threats listed in the risk register set out in Annex I: the methodology for developing and maintaining the risk register is included in NL-SYS-04; additionally, specific threats and risks are considered as a part of security problem definitions in respective Protection Profiles (NL-CS-series of documents) and audit framework documents (NLP-W/PP series of documents).
- Mapping of controls: Elaborated on in the NL-P-P/W-series – cfr the requirements on “Wallet Onboarding & LifeCycle Management” and “PID-issuance and lifecycle management).

(NL-CS-series of documents) and audit framework documents (NL-P-W/PP series of documents).

### 7.2 Conformity with (EU) Cybersecurity Act (Article 54(1) - Elements of European cybersecurity certification schemes {#s-7-2}

- 215 The NL-CS (Cybersecurity Certification Scheme) is designed to be compliant 5 with Article 54(1) of the CSA.
- 216 A European cybersecurity certification scheme shall include at least the following elements:
- 217 Subject matter and scope: The scope of the scheme is defined in the introductory section of NL-CS.
- 218 b) Purpose of the scheme: The purpose is to certify the cybersecurity of the EUDI Wallet components.
- 219 c) References to standards: For the EUCC program Common Criteria/Common Evaluation Methodology, CC/CEM:2022 release 1 (ISO/IEC 15408:2022/ISO/IEC 18045:2022, respectively) apply; for the national cybersecurity certification scheme EN 17640:2022.
- 220 d) Assurance levels: The scheme explicitly targets a high assurance level, specifically AVA\_VAN.5, for the EUCC related certifications, and assurance level “high” according to the definition contained in Regulation (EU) 2019/881 for the FITCEM related part of NL-CS (see Figure 5).

## Annex A Conformity assessment methods and techniques {#s-a}

### A.1 Terms relating to conformity assessment {#s-a-1}

NOTE: All definitions are taken from EN-ISO/IEC 17000:2020 unless otherwise stated.

- 239 Conformity assessment - demonstration that specified requirements are fulfilled
- 240 Object of conformity assessment - entity to which specified requirements apply
- 241 Specified requirement - need or expectation that is stated

NOTE to entry: Specified requirements can be stated in normative documents such as regulations, standards and technical specifications.

- 242 Conformity assessment body - body that performs conformity assessment activities, excluding accreditation
- 243 Accreditation body - body that performs accreditation
- 244 Whenever a requirement is assessed, the scheme documentation needs to identify the following elements:
- (a) Conformity assessment type. In the context of EUDI Wallet certification scheme it is a choice among the following: evaluation and its sub-types (testing, audit, inspection, validation, verification, certification (managements systems, product/service/process), accreditation.
- (b) Rationale for a choice of the method: considering the definitions of the methods and provisions of CIR (EU) 2024/2981.

### A.2 Methods relating to evaluation {#s-a-2}

- 245 NOTE: EN-ISO/IEC 17065 defines general functions “Selection” and “Determination” in joined conformity assessment activity called “Evaluation”.
- 246 Testing - determination of one or more characteristics of an object of conformity assessment, according to a procedure

NOTE: procedure is a specified way to carry out an activity or a process.

- 247 Audit - process for obtaining relevant information about an object of conformity assessment and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which specified requirements are fulfilled

NOTE entry: Examples of objects for an audit are management systems, processes, products and services.

- 248 Inspection - examination of an object of conformity assessment and determination of its conformity with detailed requirements or, based on professional judgement, with general requirements

NOTE 1 to entry: Examination can include direct or indirect observations, which can include measurements or the output of instruments.

NOTE 2 to entry (modified): Conformity assessment schemes can specify inspection as examination only.

- 249 Validation - confirmation of plausibility for a specific intended use or application through the provision of objective evidence that specified requirements have been fulfilled

NOTE to entry: Validation can be applied to claims to confirm the information declared with the claim regarding intended future use.

According to EN ISO/IEC 17029, claim is information declared by the client.

- 250 Verification - confirmation of truthfulness through the provision of objective evidence that specified requirements have been fulfilled

NOTE to entry: Verification can be applied to claims to confirm the information declared with the claim regarding events that have already occurred or results that have already been obtained.

### A.3 Various types of attestations {#s-a-3}

- 251 Attestation - issue of a statement, based on a decision, that fulfilment of specified requirements has been demonstrated
- 252 NOTE 1 to entry (modified): The resulting statement is referred as a “statement of conformity”.
- 253 NOTE 2 to entry (modified): First-party attestation is called declaration (of conformity) while third-party attestation is distinguished by the terms certification and accreditation.
- 254 Certification - third-party attestation related to an object of conformity assessment, except for accreditation
- 255 Several objects of certification are applied to the EUDI Wallet certification scheme, namely, management systems, products, services and processes.
- 256 According to EN-ISO/IEC 17021-1, Introduction: Certification of a management system provides independent demonstration that the management system of the organization:
- a) conforms to specified requirements;
- b) is capable of consistently achieving its stated policy and objectives;
- c) is effectively implemented.
- 257 According to EN-ISO/IEC 17065, Introduction: Certification of products, processes or services is a means of providing assurance that they comply with specified requirements in standards and other normative documents.
- 258 Accreditation - third-party attestation related to a conformity assessment body conveying formal demonstration of its competence, impartiality and consistent operation in performing specific conformity assessment activities.

## Annex B Description of supported Wallet Solution architectures in the Dutch national wallet certification system {#s-b}

## A. High-level diagram of EUDI Wallet solutions {#s-a-4}

Under Certification System v1 only HSM-based architectures are accepted, whereby:

- the Wallet Instance runs on a mobile platform that meet established conditions and interacts with a Wallet Provider Backend (where the HSM-based WSCA/WSCD run)
- the Wallet Instance complies with the Wallet Instance FITCEM PP and the complies with WSCA CC PP as defined under NL-CS-series are accepted.
